Stated Claim / Post Context:
'The honour of a lifetime': Carrie Leeson to leave Lifeline Canberra after 12 years

Ms Leeson wrote to Lifeline volunteers thanking them for their dedication.

Lifeline Canberra chief executive Carrie Leeson has announced she is stepping down after 12 "incredibly rewarding" years in the top job.

Login or signup to continue reading

"It has truly been the honour of a lifetime, and I leave with absolute confidence in the future," she said.

Ms Leeson wrote to Lifeline volunteers telling them first of her decision.

"Thank you for your dedication, your commitment and your kindness. Whether you have answered the phones, sorted donations, raised funds or supported our community in countless other ways, you have changed lives," she said

"You are the heart of this organisation, and it has been an absolute privilege to witness the extraordinary impact you make every day. Thank you for allowing me to be part of this remarkable journey."

Ms Leeson took on the role of CEO in 2014 but was a grassroots volunteer before then.

"As many of you know, my journey with this organisation didn't begin in the CEO's office," she wrote to the volunteers.

"It began on the phones, sitting alongside other crisis support volunteers, listening to people in their darkest moments and learning what it truly means to be there for someone in crisis.

"Those early experiences, witnessing the courage of our community, shaped my leadership and remained at the heart of every decision I have made since. Being entrusted with the custodianship of this remarkable organisation has been one of the greatest honours of my life."

Originally from South Africa, Ms Leeson said in her email that the volunteers were Lifeline's greatest strength.

"When I look back on the past 12 years, I don't think first about buildings, budgets, or balance sheets. I think about people," she said.

"I think about you, our wonderful volunteers who generously support our warehouse and fundraising events, together with the talented, passionate staff who have challenged, supported, and inspired me every step of the way. I have many many people to thank in the weeks ahead, and so many wonderful memories.

"Together, we have supported hundreds of thousands of people through crisis, strengthened our organisation, navigated COVID, expanded our services, established our sister centre in Narrm and, very soon, will celebrate answering our one millionth call - a milestone that belongs to every volunteer and every member of our team. None of this would have been possible without you.

"I leave immensely proud of what we have achieved together and deeply grateful for the friendships, memories and shared purpose that will stay with me always. It has truly been the honour of a lifetime, and I leave with absolute confidence in the future.

"The foundations are strong, our purpose is unwavering and I leave you in the hands of our incredible team."
